chunks: 5 – Jaʿfar ibn Maʿrūf, Abū al-Faḍl, al-Samarqandī. Al-ʿAyyāshī narrated from him a lot.
There was irtifāʿ (elevation/prominence) in his madhhab (school/stance). His ḥadīth is recognized sometimes, and other times rejected.

key_terms.ارْتِفَاعٌ: Irtifāʿ, meaning elevation, prominence, or high status in a specific context.
key_terms.الْعَيَّاشِيُّ: Al-ʿAyyāshī, a prominent Shia hadith scholar and biographer.
key_terms.حَدِيثُهُ: His hadith, referring to the narrations transmitted by him.
key_terms.مَذْهَبِهِ: His madhhab, referring to his school of thought or theological stance.
key_terms.يُعْرَفُ: Yuʿraf, meaning it is recognized or accepted as valid.
key_terms.يُنْكَرُ: Yunkar, meaning it is rejected or considered weak.

ai.seo_question: Who is Jaʿfar ibn Maʿrūf al-Samarqandī and what is the status of his hadith narrations?
ai.summary: This biographical entry describes Jaʿfar ibn Maʿrūf al-Samarqandī, noting that al-ʿAyyāshī narrated frequently from him. It characterizes his theological or jurisprudential stance as having 'irtifāʿ' (elevation or prominence) and notes that his narrations are sometimes accepted and sometimes rejected, indicating a mixed reliability in hadith sciences.
